value.rationale: The inverse-square adaptive reset law is a marginal localization model with physically relevant reset operation frequency. Its first finite-mean threshold (strength 2), second-moment/finite-variance threshold (strength 12), and all higher temporal moment thresholds are distinctly meaningful renewal reliability boundaries. The nontrivial exact CV²>1 formula quantifies count dispersion and shows it decreases monotonically with strength. This distinguishes an actual temporal performance observable from established stationary spatial criticality.
